text: Following them at a short distance came two elderly women of the lower middle class, one stout and ponderous, the other rosy cheeked and nimble, who were watching the old mans strange behavior with great curiosity. <break time="0.8s" /> Like most people of their station, they were fascinated by any sign of an odd mind, but they were too far off to be certain whether his gestures were merely eccentric or genuinely mad. <break time="0.8s" /> After they had scrutinized the old mans back in silence for a moment and given each other a queer, sly look, they went on energetically piecing together their very complicated dialogue. <break time="0.8s" /> Nell, Bert, Lot, Cess, Phil, Pa, he says, I says, she says, I says, I says, I says, said one, and the other answered with a list of her own, My Bert, Sis, Bill, Grandad, the old man, sugar. <break time="0.8s" /> The ponderous woman looked through the pattern of falling words at the flowers standing cool, firm, and upright in the earth, with a curious expression on her face. <break time="0.8s" /> She saw them as a sleeper waking from a heavy sleep sees a brass candlestick reflecting the light in an unfamiliar way, and she gazed at them, wide awake, with all her powers. <break time="0.8s" /> The heavy woman came to a standstill opposite the flower bed and ceased even to pretend to listen, letting the words fall over her, until she suggested that they should find a seat and have their tea. <break time="0.8s" /> Meanwhile the snail had considered every possible method of reaching its goal without going round the dead leaf or climbing over it, and it had finally decided to creep beneath it.
